details.description: Code Llama is a family of large language models for code that Meta built on top of Llama 2 and released August 24, 2023, later adding a 70B size on January 29, 2024. This is the base 34B-parameter checkpoint, trained on 500 billion tokens of code and code-related data for code completion and generation across Python, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript/JavaScript, C#, and Bash. It is the general-purpose foundation model, distinct from the Python-specialized and instruction-tuned Code Llama 34B variants Meta released alongside it.
advantages: Scores 48.8% pass@1 on HumanEval and 55.0% pass@1 on MBPP (Code Llama paper, Table 2).
Trained on 500 billion tokens of code and code-related data (Meta Code Llama blog).
Supports Python, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript/JavaScript, C#, and Bash (Meta Code Llama blog).
disadvantages: Unlike the 7B and 13B Code Llama sizes, the 34B and 70B models were not trained with fill-in-the-middle (infilling) capability (Meta Code Llama blog).
Base model without instruction-tuning; Meta's Hugging Face model card positions the separate Code Llama - Instruct variant as safer for code-assistant and chat-style use.
use_cases: Code understanding and explanation across Python, C++, Java, PHP, TypeScript/JavaScript, C#, and Bash

sources.title: Code Llama: A state-of-the-art large language model for coding
Code Llama: Open Foundation Models for Code

notes: Catalog's max_input/max_output_tokens of 16384 matches Fireworks' own listed ~16.3k-token serving context for this hosted model; Meta's paper/model card describe the family as trained on 16K-token sequences with quality improving up to 100K tokens at inference, a larger figure Fireworks does not appear to serve. No source marks Code Llama 34B deprecated or legacy as of this research.
